name: Optimus-1 (Hybrid Multimodal Memory Empowered Agents Excel in Long-Horizon Tasks)
venue: NeurIPS 2024 (Conference; accepted). Preprint: arXiv:2408.03615 (v1 7 Aug 2024, v2 21 Oct 2024). Subjects: cs.AI, cs.CL.
authors_affiliation: Zaijing Li (1,2), Yuquan Xie (1), Rui Shao (1, corresponding), Gongwei Chen (1), Dongmei Jiang (2), Liqiang Nie (1, corresponding). Affiliations: (1) Harbin Institute of Technology, Shenzhen; (2) Peng Cheng Laboratory. Group is JiuTian-VL (HITSZ).
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/JiuTian-VL/Optimus-1 also hosts/links a 'Awesome Minecraft Agents' tracking repository the authors maintain to track the latest advancements in Minecraft Agents (per repo README). [uncertain on the exact separate list URL]
task_domain: Embodied / open-world decision-making and long-horizon planning: an MLLM-based agent (Optimus-1) that perceives, plans, reflects, and acts to complete long-horizon crafting/mining tasks in Minecraft (MineRL). Combines high-level planning + reflection (MLLM) with a low-level action controller (STEVE-1). Not QA; it is interactive embodied agentic decision-making.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent embodied decision-making in Minecraft (MineRL, Minecraft 1.16.5, MineDojo-compatible craft/smelt actions). The agent runs at 20 fps in survival mode, starts with an EMPTY inventory and a random spawn point, and acts only via low-level mouse/keyboard control signals plus abstracted craft/smelt actions; observation is a raw 640x360 RGB frame (with night-vision augmentation). Long-horizon tasks require many indispensable sub-goals (e.g. ~15 sub-goals to craft a diamond sword). The MLLM (GPT-4V / open-source MLLMs) acts as Knowledge-Guided Planner and Experience-Driven Reflector; STEVE-1 acts as the low-level Action Controller. Train-free / non-parametric: the Hybrid Multimodal Memory (HDKG + AMEP) is built and grown without parameter updates. Multiple Optimus-1 instances are run in PARALLEL during memory construction (free exploration) sharing the same HDKG and AMEP, but the deployed agent is single-agent. Supervision: no fine-tuning; world knowledge is acquired via environment feedback (free exploration) plus a small set of teacher-provided task plans (teacher guidance, auto-extracted from Minecraft Wiki and ordered by GPT-4).
what_is_retrieved: Two distinct retrievable stores: (1) KNOWLEDGE - sub-graphs of crafting/mining dependencies retrieved from the Hierarchical Directed Knowledge Graph (HDKG) for the target object/task (i.e. required materials and their topologically-sorted order). (2) EXPERIENCES - multimodal historical experience cases (summarized video-frame buffers + textual sub-goal + environment/agent-state/plan metadata) retrieved from the Abstracted Multimodal Experience Pool (AMEP); both SUCCESS and FAILURE cases (the three reflection scenarios COMPLETE / CONTINUE / REPLAN) are retrieved as in-context references.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID, and in a second sense GROWING. (a) Hybrid across two memory types: a structured KNOWLEDGE store (HDKG, a directed graph of object/craft relations) plus an episodic EXPERIENCE store (AMEP). (b) Both stores are GROWING/agent-written self-built memories rather than a fixed external corpus: HDKG accumulates learned craft relations and AMEP accumulates summarized multimodal experiences, expanded online during free-exploration/teacher-guidance and during task execution (self-evolution). They are not a static external document corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Mixed by store. For HDKG: a COMPLETENESS objective - given the target object, retrieve the node, extract the full dependency sub-graph, and topologically sort it to recover the COMPLETE minimal set of prerequisite materials/sub-goals needed (so the whole plan can be generated in one shot, not iteratively). For AMEP: a precision/relevance retrieval that returns the single most-relevant case PER scenario (COMPLETE, CONTINUE, REPLAN) as reference (effectively a small per-category top-1, not a fixed large top-k ranking). [uncertain on exact AMEP retrieval k]
cbr_cycle_coverage: [Retrieve: yes, Reuse: yes, Revise: partial, Retain: yes]. Retrieve: AMEP cases (success+failure) are retrieved by relevance during reflection; HDKG sub-graphs retrieved for planning. Reuse: retrieved experiences used as in-context demonstrations to judge current state; retrieved knowledge reused to generate the plan. Revise: the reflector's REPLAN outcome triggers the Knowledge-Guided Planner to REVISE the plan (plan-level revision), but individual retrieved cases are not edited/adapted. Retain: successful AND failed experiences are written back to AMEP, and newly-learned craft relations are written to HDKG (Retain).
explicit_cbr_grounding: False - the paper does NOT frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner. It is grounded in cognitive-science long-term memory theory (semantic vs episodic memory; knowledge vs experience), in-context learning, knowledge graphs, and agent memory literature. It nonetheless realizes Retrieve/Reuse/Retain (and plan-level Revise) CBR-like mechanisms under the 'memory / experience pool' framing.
retrieval_unit: Two granularities by store. (1) KG-subgraph: from HDKG, a directed dependency sub-graph 𝒟j(𝒱j,ℰj) for the target object, topologically sorted into an ordered list of (material, quantity) prerequisites. (2) Multimodal experience case: from AMEP, a summarized experience = an abstracted 16-frame image buffer (visual memory) aligned to a textual sub-goal via MineCLIP, plus environment information, agent initial state, and the plan; retrieved per reflection scenario (COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN). So the unit ranges from a structured KG sub-graph (knowledge) to a summarized multimodal episodic case (experience).
index_source: Growing, agent-written memory (hybrid construction). HDKG and AMEP are built non-parametrically by the agent via 'free exploration - teacher guidance': free exploration writes learned craft relations (HDKG) and success+failure experiences (AMEP) from environment feedback; teacher guidance adds a small number of long-horizon task plans (auto-extracted from Minecraft Wiki, ordered by GPT-4). During deployment AMEP also continues to be updated after each task (online growth / self-evolution across epochs). Not an offline static corpus.
index_structure_topology: Two structures. (1) HDKG: a hierarchical DIRECTED knowledge GRAPH 𝒟(𝒱,ℰ) where nodes are objects and directed edges point to objects craftable/obtainable from them; retrieval is node-lookup + sub-graph extraction + topological sort; ~851 objects (nodes) fit in <1 MB and updates are local (M+N ops for M nodes, N edges). (2) AMEP: an experience pool keyed by sub-goal text and indexed/aligned via MineCLIP video-text similarity, organized by the three reflection scenarios (COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN); content is summarized (video buffer 1 fps -> image buffer window=16 -> similarity-pruned frames). So topology = dependency graph (knowledge) + similarity/metadata-keyed pool (experience).
retriever_type: Hybrid / heterogeneous across stores. (1) HDKG: symbolic graph retrieval - exact node lookup then sub-graph extraction and topological sort (not a vector retriever). (2) AMEP: multimodal similarity retrieval using MineCLIP (a CLIP-like pre-trained video-text alignment model) to compute visual-content vs sub-goal correlation for summarization and to retrieve the most relevant cases; the MLLM (planner/reflector) consumes the retrieved knowledge/experience. No BM25; no learned/trained dense retriever beyond off-the-shelf MineCLIP.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf / train-free). HDKG retrieval is symbolic (no learning). AMEP uses a pre-trained, frozen MineCLIP video-text alignment model for visual-text correlation/retrieval with no fine-tuning. The overall Hybrid Multimodal Memory is explicitly 'non-parametric' / 'train-free' - no contrastive, LM-feedback, preference, or RL signal is used to train the retriever. (Memory CONTENTS grow via environment feedback success/failure, but the retriever itself is not trained.)
query_construction: Store-specific. (1) HDKG query: the target task/object name x (e.g. 'diamond sword'); the planner retrieves its node and the dependency sub-graph (raw object identity as key). (2) AMEP query: the current task plus the agent's current multimodal state - the current observation/state pair and sub-goal - matched against stored experiences via MineCLIP video-text similarity, retrieving the most relevant COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN cases. No synthetic query rewriting or decomposition of the query itself (the HDKG itself provides task decomposition).
query_granularity: Both task-level and step/sub-goal-level. HDKG retrieval is task-level (one-shot at plan time, key = target object). AMEP retrieval is sub-goal/state-level: the Experience-Driven Reflector queries periodically during execution conditioned on the current sub-goal and current visual state. So planning uses one task-level knowledge retrieval, reflection uses repeated sub-goal/state-level experience retrieval.
when_to_retrieve: Mixed schedule. Knowledge (HDKG): one-shot at plan time (retrieve once to build the complete plan, avoiding iterative per-step planning). Experience (AMEP): iterative on a fixed periodic schedule - the Experience-Driven Reflector is 'periodically activated' / 'activates at regular intervals' during sub-goal execution to retrieve experiences and decide COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN. Not uncertainty-triggered or learned-router-gated.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Fixed/scheduled triggers tied to the control loop. (1) HDKG retrieval triggered once when a (re)plan is generated by the Knowledge-Guided Planner. (2) AMEP retrieval triggered by the periodic activation of the Experience-Driven Reflector at regular time/step intervals during sub-goal execution; the reflector's REPLAN verdict then re-triggers planning (and thus HDKG retrieval). No token-confidence/attention/reflection-token learned trigger; periodicity is a hyperparameter. [uncertain on exact reflection interval]
reranking: None - no explicit cross-encoder/RRF/hierarchy-aware reranking stage. HDKG returns the dependency sub-graph directly (ordered by topological sort, which acts as a deterministic ordering rather than a learned rerank). AMEP returns the most-relevant case(s) per scenario by MineCLIP similarity without a second-stage reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Summarization/compression is the dominant refinement, applied at WRITE time so retrieved items are already abstracted: AMEP performs static (1 fps video-buffer filtering) + dynamic (16-frame image buffer with similarity-based pruning) summarization and MineCLIP threshold-gated alignment, yielding compact 'abstracted' multimodal experiences (vs JARVIS-1 which stores raw un-summarized history). HDKG refines knowledge into a topologically-sorted ordered material list. At READ time, retrieved knowledge is recomposed into the plan prompt and retrieved experiences are selected per scenario; no separate distractor-filtering/decompose-recompose module beyond this.
tool_document_engineering: N/A - no tool/API descriptions are indexed. The low-level skills are produced by a single fixed action controller (STEVE-1); there is no tool-document store, so no docstring/synthetic-query/weighted-field engineering.
index_content_separation: Partial / present in spirit. AMEP deliberately separates a lightweight, summarized index (abstracted 16-frame buffers + sub-goal text + metadata) from the heavy raw video stream, explicitly to improve storage and retrieval efficiency vs storing all frames (JARVIS-1). HDKG stores compact symbolic nodes/edges (<1MB for 851 nodes) rather than heavy content. This is an efficiency-driven index-vs-content abstraction, though not a formal progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content protocol.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A as a tool-retrieval system. HDKG is a live, incrementally-updatable knowledge graph (add M nodes / N edges with M+N local operations; auto-extracted craft relations from Minecraft Wiki). There is no RapidAPI/REST/MCP/function-calling tool protocol; the agent interacts with the environment via low-level mouse/keyboard actions plus abstracted craft/smelt actions through MineRL.
tool_dependency_awareness: Not for tools, but YES for object/material dependencies. HDKG explicitly models inter-OBJECT crafting/mining dependencies (output-of-A enables B; e.g. wooden pickaxe -> mine stone -> stone pickaxe -> mine iron, etc.) as a directed dependency graph, and topological sorting recovers prerequisite ordering. This is a dependency-graph mechanism over craft prerequisites rather than over callable tools/APIs.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation (in-context). (1) Retrieved HDKG knowledge (topologically-sorted craft graph) is injected into the Knowledge-Guided Planner prompt (alongside the task and the raw visual observation) to generate the full sub-goal sequence in one shot. (2) Retrieved AMEP experiences (success+failure cases for COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN) are injected into the Experience-Driven Reflector prompt to perform in-context-learning reflection on the current state and decide COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN. No weight updates (train-free); retrieved content drives planning and reflection only via prompting.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan + per-period interleaved reflect-then-replan. Pipeline: (i) Knowledge-Guided Planner senses the visual observation, retrieves HDKG knowledge, and decomposes the task into an executable sub-goal sequence in ONE shot (knowledge-guided plan-at-once, contrasted with iterative step-by-step planning of MP5/Voyager); (ii) Action Controller (STEVE-1) executes sub-goals sequentially; (iii) Experience-Driven Reflector periodically retrieves AMEP experiences to classify the situation (COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN) and, on REPLAN, sends the agent back to the planner to revise the plan. No MCTS/tree search; retrieval is woven in at the plan step (knowledge) and at periodic reflection points (experience).
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-sub-goal / per-reflection-period within a rollout. Knowledge retrieval is once per (re)plan; experience retrieval + reflection occurs periodically during sub-goal execution (per execution interval), not per CoT token. So interleaving is at the planning event and at periodic sub-goal-level reflection events.
adaptation_mechanism: Plan-level execution-feedback-driven revision rather than per-case adaptation. Retrieved AMEP experiences are used as verbatim multimodal ICL exemplars (not edited per case); however, the Experience-Driven Reflector's REPLAN verdict - informed by retrieved success+failure cases and current visual state - triggers the Knowledge-Guided Planner to REVISE/regenerate the plan (HDKG-grounded), i.e. critic/feedback-guided revision at the plan level. No RL-reuse-finetuning or latent adaptation; retrieved knowledge sub-graphs are reused as-is to construct the revised plan.
retrieved_item_representation: Two surface forms. (1) Knowledge: a structured, topologically-sorted craft graph / ordered (material, quantity) list rendered into the planner prompt (structured note). (2) Experience: an abstracted multimodal case = summarized video frames (visual memory) + textual sub-goal + environment/agent-state/plan metadata, injected as multimodal in-context demonstrations (success and failure references). Not raw full trajectories (summarized), not executable programs, not latent tokens.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Abstracted, mid-level on both axes. Knowledge from HDKG is a high-level structured dependency/recipe representation (semantic knowledge, a reusable craft-relation graph). Experience from AMEP is a SUMMARIZED/abstracted multimodal case (not a raw trajectory) - it preserves global overview + local details while compressing the frame stream. So retrieved units are distilled/abstracted (knowledge sub-graph + abstracted experience), deliberately more abstract than raw trajectories yet more concrete than free-text strategies.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Reflection-based self-assessment plus contrastive success+failure references and summarization. The Experience-Driven Reflector retrieves both successful and FAILED cases (COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN) to help judge the current state and catch errors, enabling correction/replanning (the inclusion of failure cases is shown by ablation to improve robustness). AMEP summarization (MineCLIP threshold-gated, similarity-pruned buffers) reduces redundant/low-information visual content. HDKG provides correct symbolic prerequisites reducing planning hallucination. No retriever-aware SFT or distractor-aware training (train-free).
memory_type: Hybrid: graph memory (HDKG, semantic/structured world knowledge) + episodic multimodal experience memory (AMEP, summarized success and failure cases). Plug-and-play, non-parametric (textual/structured form, not parametric).
write_back: True. Newly-learned craft/mining relations are written into HDKG (e.g. {3 planks, 2 sticks -> wooden pickaxe} added on success); summarized multimodal experiences - including FAILURE cases (REPLAN feedback) - are written into AMEP during and after task execution. Memory is updated after each task and grows across self-evolution epochs.
online_growth: True. The Hybrid Multimodal Memory grows during deployment/self-evolution: starting from an empty memory, Optimus-1 iterates 'free exploration - teacher guidance' learning and unseen-task inference, expanding HDKG (knowledge) and AMEP (experiences) each epoch (paper runs 4 epochs, 160 learning tasks per period: 150 free-exploration + 10 teacher-guidance), with success rate on unseen tasks increasing over epochs. AMEP is also updated after each task at inference. Multiple parallel Optimus-1 instances share and fill the same memory to grow it efficiently.
write_back_trigger: On-success-AND-failure. HDKG: a craft relation is written on environment-confirmed SUCCESS of an atomic craft/operation (failed free-exploration attempts may yield no new knowledge). AMEP: experiences are written for both successful sub-goals and FAILURE cases - explicitly, visual memories are stored as failure cases when the reflection feedback is REPLAN; memory is also updated after the task finishes. So writes occur on success (knowledge + experience) and on failure (experience), per sub-goal / per task rather than human-validated.
failure_experience_usage: Success + failure, used as contrastive in-context references. A core contribution: unlike JARVIS-1 which stores only successful cases, AMEP stores BOTH successful and failed cases, and the Experience-Driven Reflector retrieves the most relevant case from each of COMPLETE / CONTINUE / REPLAN to better assess the current state. Ablation (Table 3) shows retrieving both success and failure cases (97.49/94.26/53.33/11.54/9.59 on Wood/Stone/Iron/Gold/Diamond) beats success-only, failure-only, or zero-case retrieval, confirming failure cases meaningfully improve performance.
memory_evolution_update: Append-and-merge growth. HDKG is updated by locally merging new nodes/edges into the graph (M+N operations for M nodes/N edges) - append/merge, not full rewrite. AMEP appends summarized experiences (after on-the-fly summarization/pruning of the frame buffer at write time). Across self-evolution epochs the stores monotonically expand (continuous memory expansion). No explicit global forget-prune/refine-overwrite of already-stored entries is described (the pruning is at the frame-summarization step before storage). [uncertain on any eviction policy for the experience pool]
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/case-selection is NOT a learned/RL-optimized policy. HDKG retrieval is symbolic node-lookup + topological sort; AMEP retrieval is fixed off-the-shelf MineCLIP similarity selecting the most-relevant case per scenario. The entire Hybrid Multimodal Memory is explicitly non-parametric/train-free, with no soft-Q/M-MDP/RL retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: Yes, within the same framework (shared memory across parallel instances). During memory construction, multiple Optimus-1 instances are initialized and SHARE the same HDKG and AMEP, filling the memory efficiently in parallel. The Hybrid Multimodal Memory is also plug-and-play / model-agnostic: the same memory drives different MLLM backbones (GPT-4V, DeepSeek-VL, InternLM-XComposer2-VL), so memory is portable across heterogeneous MLLM planners/reflectors. It is not a multi-agent cooperative deployment; sharing is across homogeneous parallel instances / swappable backbones.
benchmarks: Primary: a self-constructed Minecraft long-horizon benchmark of 67 tasks in 7 groups (Wood/Wooden, Stone, Iron, Gold/Golden, Diamond, Redstone, Armor), evaluated in MineRL (Minecraft 1.16.5, survival, empty initial inventory, random spawn). Overall headline groups Iron/Gold/Diamond/Redstone/Armor. Additional comparisons on the benchmarks of DEPS (8 META-TASK groups MT1-MT8) and MP5 (process-dependent / tech-tree tasks), and reference to Voyager's setting (Appendix F.2). Ablation uses an 18-task subset.
benchmark_family: Embodied / open-world (Minecraft) under the survey's embodied family (ALFWorld/ScienceWorld/VirtualHome/Minecraft). Long-horizon crafting/mining decision-making with low-level action control.
baselines: GPT-3.5 (text-only, no memory), GPT-4V (zero-shot MLLM, no Hybrid Multimodal Memory), DEPS (Wang et al. 2023, Describe-Explain-Plan-Select), and JARVIS-1 (Wang et al. 2023, memory-augmented multimodal agent) on the 67-task long-horizon benchmark; plus a Human-level baseline (10 volunteers, each task played 10 times, >=20h Minecraft experience, $25 reward). Additional cross-benchmark baselines: MP5 (CVPR 2024), and on DEPS's benchmark: InnerMonologue, Code-as-Policy, DEPS. Generalization study uses DeepSeek-VL and InternLM-XComposer2-VL as MLLM backbones. Action controller is STEVE-1 (also the no-reflection comparison in Fig.4). Note: Optimus-1 starts with EMPTY inventory while DEPS/JARVIS-1 start with tools, making Optimus-1's setting harder.
key_metrics: Average Success Rate (SR, %, primary), Average number of Steps (AS, lower=better), and Average Time (AT, seconds, lower=better) per task group; +infinity denotes inability to complete. Each task evaluated >=30 times across different world seeds. Reported per group and Overall (mean over Iron/Gold/Diamond/Redstone/Armor).
headline_result: Optimus-1 significantly outperforms all existing agents and approaches human-level. On the 67-task benchmark, vs JARVIS-1 it improves SR by 29.28% (Diamond) and 53.40% (Redstone, relative). Group SRs (Optimus-1 vs JARVIS-1, with Human-level): Wood 98.60 vs 93.76 (Human 100); Stone 92.35 vs 89.20 (100); Iron 46.69 vs 36.15 (86.00); Gold 8.51 vs 7.20 (17.31); Diamond 11.61 vs 8.98 (16.98); Redstone 25.02 vs 16.31 (33.27); Armor 19.47 vs 15.82 (28.48). Overall SR 22.26 (Optimus-1) vs 16.89 (JARVIS-1) vs 5.39 (DEPS) vs 0.00 (GPT-3.5/GPT-4V), with Human-level 36.41. With Hybrid Multimodal Memory, open-source MLLM-based Optimus-1 shows 2x-6x improvement, surpassing the GPT-4V baseline on many tasks; up to ~30% improvement over existing agents.
ablations: (1) Module ablation (Table 2, P=Planning, R=Reflection, K=Knowledge/HDKG, E=Experience/AMEP) on 5 groups: bare 14.29/0/0/0/0 (Wood..Diamond); +P 42.95/25.67/0/0/0; +P+R 55.00/47.37/18.11/2.08/1.11; +P+R+E 73.53/64.20/24.19/3.08/1.86; +P+R+K 92.37/69.63/38.33/3.49/2.42; full +P+R+K+E 97.49/94.26/53.33/11.54/9.59. Removing HDKG drops SR by ~20% on average; removing AMEP drops ~12%. (2) AMEP retrieval mode (Table 3): Zero-case 92.00/79.26/36.32/4.25/3.25; Success-only 95.00/84.29/46.98/9.36/7.89; Failure-only 95.00/81.10/45.47/7.50/6.39; Success+Failure (full) 97.49/94.26/53.33/11.54/9.59 - not retrieving cases costs ~10% on average; success+failure is best. (3) Generalization (Fig.5a): DeepSeek-VL / InternLM-XComposer2-VL gain 2-6x with memory. (4) Self-evolution (Fig.5b): SR rises over 4 epochs.
evaluation_decoupling: No. The paper reports only end-to-end task metrics (SR, AS, AT) and does not report intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / retrieval completeness) decoupled from task performance. Retrieval quality is assessed indirectly via the HDKG/AMEP ablations on downstream SR.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome (final task SR), with efficiency-as-process proxies: Average Steps (AS) and Average Time (AT) capture HOW efficiently the agent reaches the goal (Optimus-1 has lower AS/AT than baselines, indicating better process efficiency, e.g. one-shot vs iterative planning). The reflector's COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN classification is an intermediate process signal but its accuracy is not separately scored. No reasoning-faithfulness or step-wise retrieval-accuracy metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Efficiency is a headline claim. One-shot knowledge-guided planning (HDKG) avoids the time-consuming iterative step-by-step planning of MP5/Voyager (Fig.13 shows iterative planners endanger the agent while replanning). AMEP summarization reduces storage/retrieval cost vs JARVIS-1's raw-history storage; HDKG with 851 nodes is <1 MB and updates in M+N local ops. Optimus-1 achieves lower Average Steps (AS) and Average Time (AT) than all baselines across groups. Compute/cost: experiments on 4x NVIDIA A100 80G GPUs; non-API learning (free exploration + teacher guidance) ~16 hours, inference ~20 hours; ~$5,000 total spent on GPT-4V API; open-source MLLM backbones offered as low-cost alternatives with comparable performance.
context_budget_and_selection_count: AMEP injects a small, summarized set: per reflection it retrieves the most-relevant case from each of the three scenarios (COMPLETE/CONTINUE/REPLAN), and visual experiences are bounded by an image buffer window size of 16 frames (video buffer filters to 1 fps; MineCLIP threshold gates storage). HDKG injects the full topologically-sorted prerequisite list for the target task (size = task dependency depth). No fixed token-budget cap is reported; selection is relevance/threshold-driven and buffer-window-capped rather than a large fixed top-k. [uncertain on exact AMEP retrieval count and token budget]
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A - Optimus-1 is a method/agent paper, not a survey/taxonomy.
benchmark_construction_and_size: Self-constructed Minecraft long-horizon benchmark: 67 tasks across 7 groups (Wooden 10, Stone 9, Iron 16, Golden 6, Redstone 6, Diamond 7, Armor 13), categorized by recommended Minecraft categories. Per-task Max. Steps scaled to human completion time (3600-36000 steps); empty initial inventory; avg sub-goals per group range 4.60 (Wood) to 17.50 (Redstone). Diamond spawn probability adjusted to 20% (levels 2-16) for both agent and humans to reduce variance. Each task run >=30 times with different world seeds; outcome auto-verifiable via Minecraft inventory/environment feedback. Difficulty signaled by best-system (Optimus-1) Overall SR 22.26 vs Human-level 36.41 (large remaining gap, esp. Gold/Diamond).
builds_on: JARVIS-1 (Wang et al. 2023, memory-augmented multimodal LLM agent - direct predecessor for multimodal experience memory, which Optimus-1 improves by summarizing experiences and adding failure cases); STEVE-1 (Lifshitz et al. 2023, used directly as the low-level Action Controller); MineCLIP (Fan et al. 2022 / MineDojo, used as the frozen video-text alignment summarizer/retriever); MineRL (Guss et al. 2019, environment); GPT-4V (planner/reflector backbone); DEPS (Wang et al. 2023, interactive planning); VPT (Baker et al. 2022). Conceptually grounded in cognitive-science long-term memory (semantic vs episodic) and agent-memory literature.
contrasts_with: JARVIS-1 (stores ALL multimodal history without summarization and only successful cases -> Optimus-1 summarizes into AMEP and adds failure cases); MP5 and Voyager (iterative, time-consuming step-by-step planning and/or text-converted visual descriptions; Voyager/DEPS/MP5 act via code/APIs in Mineflayer/MineDojo -> Optimus-1 uses one-shot knowledge-guided planning over a directed graph, direct visual conditioning, and low-level human-like mouse/keyboard control in MineRL with empty inventory); GPT-3.5/GPT-4V (no knowledge/experience memory); fine-tuning-based knowledge learning (MineDreamer etc.) -> Optimus-1 learns explicitly and train-free via HDKG.
lineage: Group C (RAG + planning), at the intersection of retrieval-augmented planning and experiential/graph memory agents. Lineage: video/IL+RL Minecraft policies (VPT, MineCLIP, STEVE-1) -> LLM/MLLM planners with memory (Voyager, DEPS, MP5, JARVIS-1) -> Optimus-1, which fuses a structured directed knowledge graph (HDKG, semantic/world knowledge for one-shot planning) with an abstracted multimodal experience pool (AMEP, episodic success+failure cases for reflection), establishing a hybrid knowledge+experience memory for long-horizon embodied agents. Successors: Optimus-2 and Optimus-3 (same JiuTian-VL group).
